account:
Today I have followed my appointments: morning office hours, the mill grain inspection, lunch at home, and council letters. No letters or new appointment requests reached the secretary. At the mill I obtained no clear supply information, so I have asked the secretary to seek a factual report from the miller for my sixteen-thirty return. I am now early for fifteen o'clock tea at the neighbour's dockside cottage.

The unusual thread is repeated news of the baker and innkeeper together, and the innkeeper carrying sacks of bread at the bakery, market, and plaza. Yesterday there were also reports of the baker carrying bread at the inn. Several townsfolk repeat a vague 'bridge or port change at bakery' report, but I do not understand what actual event it describes. The secretary says the baker crossed the plaza bridge safely this morning and knew of no disruption, so I have no confirmed evidence of a crossing problem.

The innkeeper has arranged an eighteen o'clock presentation today in the great hall involving local baking and hospitality, with participating tradespeople. He said I need make no preparations. My best guess is that the bread movements and cooperation concern preparations for that presentation, perhaps refreshments or a demonstration. The baker and innkeeper are clearly involved; the neighbour was mentioned in one report, but I have not established their part. I feel there may be activity being organised without my knowing its details, but I cannot yet say it is secret or improper. Separately, the town's old financial ledger remains missing, with income and obligations unknown; I have no evidence connecting that problem to the bread or presentation.
